From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-13T09:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Realtime API errors + throughput drop — urgent exec/infra loop

Quick triage update:
- Autoscaler showed an anomalous delay in spin-up for one Dedicated pool (d-pool-7) between 08:40–08:52 PT; health-check flapped briefly.
- Network egress to us-west-2 had a short routing asymmetry; packets routed through a different AZ for ~7m.
- We temporarily routed Bronco traffic to cold-standby pool (d-pool-12) at 09:26 PT and observed immediate reduction in 500s; throughput recovered to ~85% of baseline.

Next actions:
1) Keep traffic on d-pool-12 and monitor for 30m.
2) Post-mortem on d-pool-7 spin-up path; verify autoscaler retry/config.
3) Laura/Rishi to validate whether any request patterns during the window could have exacerbated KV cache misses.

No customer-facing language yet — Marissa, if you can confirm we've got the temporary mitigation and a short impact summary, I'll prepare infra notes for the post-mortem.

— Vivek
VP, Infrastructure

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-13T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Realtime API errors + throughput drop — urgent exec/infra loop

Triage from model-serving side:
- No new model rollouts in the last 48h for BRN-9521. The model variant in production is stable (v2.3-q4).
- Telemetry shows increased KV cache miss rate starting 08:42 PT coincident with the AZ routing change Vivek noted. Miss rate rose from 6% -> 28% for Bronco's longest-prefix keys.
- A correlation: many requests had longer prefix lengths than usual (customer reported a batch of synthetic load runs at 08:30 PT). KV miss spikes would cause more compute and longer per-request latency, exposing the autoscaler spin-up gap.

Action items:
- Rishi to draft a targeted config tweak (shorter prefix TTL for this customer) to reduce cache pressure while we stabilize routing.
- I'll add an exec summary of impact and recommended mitigation for the post-mortem.

Laura
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-13T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Bronco status update — temporary mitigation in place

Hi Elena / Marco —

Thanks for flagging this. Quick update from our side: we observed a throughput regression and intermittent 500s starting ~08:45 PT. We've routed your traffic to a verified standby pool which restored most traffic by 09:26 PT.

Impact summary:
- Scope: Realtime inference endpoint for checkout service (affects ~25% of user requests during window).
- Customer-visible: timeouts and errors for a subset of requests, highest latency ~12s.
- Mitigation: traffic routed to standby pool (d-pool-12). Throughput recovered to ~85% baseline; we've paused autoscaler changes to the affected pool while we investigate.

Next steps we will complete in the next 6–12 hours:
- Redwood will keep traffic on the standby pool and monitor closely (Vivek/infra).
- Engineering will apply a temporary prefix TTL reduction to reduce KV cache misses (Laura/Rishi).
- We will prepare a full incident note and post-mortem once the root cause is confirmed.

If you want a call, we can join a 30m bridge now or at 11:00 PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-03-14T17:40:00-07:00
Subject: Bronco — executive update and request for patience

Elena / Marco —

Wanted to close out the executive-side update for today. Short summary:
- Root cause hypothesis: autoscaler spin-up gap in d-pool-7 combined with an unusual burst of long-prefix requests that increased KV cache miss pressure. This led to higher-than-expected per-request CPU and memory pressure and created a transient window where requests hit overloaded nodes and returned 500s.
- Current state: Traffic remains on standby pool (d-pool-12). Latency and error rates are within acceptable bounds for production (observed error rate <0.7% over the last 6h).
- Customer impact: We estimate Bronco saw a 3–4 hour partial degradation window; we will quantify token-level impact in the post-mortem.

Commitments:
1) Formal post-mortem within 48 hours including: timeline, root cause, remediation, and actions to prevent recurrence.
2) We will propose an SLA credit if the quantification shows material impact relative to your committed SLO.
3) Short-term product change: defend autoscaler against AZ routing asymmetry with a faster cold-standby ramp and an alert for KV-miss correlated spikes.

Please let me know if you want an exec-to-exec call; happy to set one up tomorrow. Appreciate your patience while we finish the post-mortem.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

On behalf of the Redwood incident response team
